tips.activityTab.text: The Activity tab has a tab per running agent: its card, its turn and tool call, its background tasks, subagents and processes. It opens as a snapshot; Play follows it live. An agent's ⋯ menu opens it on that agent.
tips.activityTab.title: See what each agent is running
tips.activityWorkspace.text: Activity, in the activity bar, shows every project's running agents together, their tabs grouped by project. A card in progress opens it on the agents working on that card, and a run or a lane in the Progress panel on its agents (Show in Activity).
tips.activityWorkspace.title: Everything running, in one place
tips.advancedSettings.text: After a coding agent's update, Combwork no longer sees its trust question or its sign-in errors? Settings → Advanced has the text and fields Combwork looks for, and its timeouts: change one, with the default beside it, or edit advanced.json.
tips.advancedSettings.title: Fix a CLI change yourself
tips.agentConsole.text: Settings → Agent API → Let agents read the developer console gives agents a read-only tool showing their CLI's hooks and status line next to what Combwork made of each, redacted, so they can debug what Combwork sees.
tips.agentConsole.title: Let agents see what their CLI sends
tips.agentHooks.text: Hooks… in an agent's ⋯ menu lists the hooks its session has, yours too, and the last hooks Combwork received: what Combwork replied, and whether it applied or ignored each one and why.
tips.agentHooks.title: See why an agent's hooks went quiet
tips.agentInSlot.text: Beside an agent's name on its pane: in slot-b while it builds a card in a slot (click it for Branches & remotes), carried: hb2 in the slot kept for it, home: hr4 for a reviewer's retired home. The project's hover lists them in a Slot column.
tips.agentInSlot.title: See where each agent works
tips.agentLayouts.text: Each agent has its own pane: choose a layout at the right of the session toolbar, and drag a pane by its header to rearrange them. File locks stop two agents editing the same file.
tips.agentLayouts.title: Several agents side by side
tips.agentMenu.text: An agent's pane header keeps to its state, its card and Stop. Compact, Hand Over, Merge…, its settings and anything that needs a look (a dot on ⋯ says so) are in its ⋯ menu, or right-click the header. {key}
tips.agentMenu.title: Everything else is under an agent's ⋯
tips.agentSettings.text: Click an agent's model in its footer for Agent Settings: give a reviewer a faster model while another agent codes with the strongest.
tips.agentSettings.title: A model per agent
tips.agentStates.text: Each agent has one of four states, told apart by shape as well as colour: a diamond waits for you, a square is stalled, a pulsing dot is working and a ring is idle. The project header counts them: "1 waiting · 2 working".
tips.agentStates.title: Read your agents at a glance
tips.agentWorkflowRole.text: Each agent's Role in the workflow, in Agent Settings, says whether it builds cards, reviews them, or either. Start Lane offers builders and reviewers by it.
tips.agentWorkflowRole.title: Builders and reviewers
tips.agentsTempFolder.text: Agents write scripts and other temporary files to Windows' Temp folder as they work. Set Settings → Advanced → Agents' temp folder to a folder of your own, such as one you exclude from antivirus scans, and each agent gets a folder there instead.
tips.agentsTempFolder.title: Keep agents' temp files out of Windows' Temp
tips.allKeysToCli.text: In an agent's pane, Combwork's shortcuts take their keys. Turn on Settings → Advanced → All keys go to the CLI to send every key to the CLI instead, but the command palette's (Show All Commands), so every command is still in reach.
tips.allKeysToCli.title: Give every key to the agent's CLI
tips.alwaysOnTop.text: The pin in the title bar (or Ctrl+Alt+O) keeps the window above your other apps, so a test run or an emulator can work underneath. Each window has its own, remembered for its workspace.
tips.alwaysOnTop.title: Keep a Combwork window on top
tips.antivirus.text: On Windows, Microsoft Defender scans every file builds, tests and git touch. Settings → Workspace → Antivirus scanning shows whether it scans your workspace and can exclude its folders, with your consent.
tips.antivirus.title: Antivirus and your workspace
tips.archiveNew.text: The cheapest way to carry on after a long session: archive it and start clean, so nothing old is re-cached. Write a handover first so the new one knows where to pick up.
tips.archiveNew.title: Archive and Start New
tips.assistant.text: The panel on the right oversees the workspace: ask what the agents are doing, what things cost, or for a plan. {key}
tips.assistant.title: Ask the Assistant
tips.assistantAgentRequests.text: An agent that needs something only the Assistant or you can do on a card, such as parking a card On Hold on your answer, asks the Assistant directly instead of leaving a comment. The request wakes it, and it acts only within its Control and what you decided.
tips.assistantAgentRequests.title: Agents can ask the Assistant
tips.assistantBatch.text: The Assistant can move or label up to {cards, plural, one {# card} other {# cards}} in one step, each card still listed on its own.
tips.assistantBatch.title: Many cards in one step
tips.assistantCompact.text: The Assistant usually works with a bigger context than your agents, so its Compact button turns orange later: past {tokens, plural, one {# token} other {# tokens}} by default. Settings → Assistant → Highlight Compact over changes that, or Never turns it off.
tips.assistantCompact.title: When the Assistant suggests compacting
tips.assistantConnection.text: Assistant Settings → Connection picks the setup it runs on, for this workspace: keep it on your agents' model and effort, since a lighter one makes it careless. A server account such as DeepSeek works too, with caveats the guide lists.
tips.assistantConnection.title: Choose what the Assistant runs on
tips.assistantControl.text: Settings → Assistant → Control decides what it may do: only advise, or also add, start and brief agents and start cards when you ask.
tips.assistantControl.title: Let the Assistant run agents
tips.assistantImages.text: The Assistant view's Attachments shows every screenshot and file you've pasted or dropped into its conversations, by conversation. Click a conversation's name to read it again.
tips.assistantImages.title: What you've attached to the Assistant
tips.assistantJournal.text: The Assistant keeps a journal in each workspace: decisions, plans and what happened, recalled a few lines at a time after a restart. Settings → Assistant → Journal chooses what it may store, or turns it off.
tips.assistantJournal.title: The Assistant remembers
tips.assistantJournalBrowser.text: The Assistant view's Journal shows what the Assistant keeps in its journal, newest first. Search it, open an entry to correct or delete it, or use Forget These… to remove everything a search finds.
tips.assistantJournalBrowser.title: Read what the Assistant remembers
tips.assistantLaneWatch.text: Running several lanes, the Assistant waits on all of them at once and is woken only for a failed review, a blocked or stalled card, a lane ready to merge or one that ended.
tips.assistantLaneWatch.title: One watch for all the lanes
tips.assistantLanes.text: When the Assistant starts an agent on its next set of cards, it gives it a new conversation in the same step (the old one stays in the Sessions tab). Short conversations cost much less: ask it to do the same for any new card.
tips.assistantLanes.title: A new conversation for each lane
tips.assistantMcp.textAdded: The Assistant gets a workspace MCP server only once you add it for it, as for a project: + in MCP Servers in its view on the activity bar, or tick Assistant in Add to… in the MCP view. A server with your own notes can reach it and no project.
tips.assistantMcp.title: MCP servers for the Assistant only
tips.assistantMemory.text: Besides its journal, the Assistant's coding agent saves notes of its own about working with you. Memory in the Assistant view on the activity bar lists them, MEMORY.md first: open one to read or correct it.
tips.assistantMemory.title: See what the Assistant's coding agent remembers
tips.assistantMessages.text: The Assistant can't give a waiting or working agent a new task, but it can leave it a message, such as your answer: delivered as soon as the agent can take it. Its pane shows it as unread (✉) until then; click that to cancel it.
tips.assistantMessages.title: The Assistant can reach a busy agent
tips.assistantNoticeOpens.text: A notification from the Assistant or an agent about one agent or one card opens it when you click it: the agent's pane, or the card. Older ones are in the Notifications panel, and open from there too.
tips.assistantNoticeOpens.title: Click a notification to go to it
tips.assistantReplies.text: When you answer an agent in its pane while the Assistant watches it or its card, the Assistant is told the first line, so it doesn't ask you again. Settings → General → Your name sets how it names you; Settings → Assistant turns it off.
tips.assistantReplies.title: The Assistant hears your answers to agents
tips.assistantSettings.text: Not sure which setting would help? Ask the Assistant: it explains any of them and says where it is. With Settings → Assistant → Control → Change settings on, it can make the change, which you can revert from its panel.
tips.assistantSettings.title: Ask the Assistant about a setting
tips.assistantSide.text: Windows notifications or another app covering the right of the screen? View → Move Assistant Panel to the Left puts the Assistant beside the project list.
tips.assistantSide.title: The Assistant on the left
tips.assistantStatus.text: The line under the Assistant's header says what it is doing, and which cards it waits on and until when: click one to open it. Done by the Assistant at its end lists what it did. Under Workspace, hover an agent's mark for what it's doing; click to go there.
tips.assistantStatus.title: What the Assistant is doing
tips.assistantTeam.text: With three or more agents, or builders and reviewers, ask the Assistant in Coordinator mode to run your cards as lanes: it splits them by the files they touch, briefs each pair and watches every lane to the end. With one or two agents it keeps out of the way.
tips.assistantTeam.title: The Assistant runs your team
tips.assistantTemplates.text: Ask the Assistant to load a template into a project, naming any agent you like: it shows what would change first, applies the template's workflow, and Undo puts the old agents back.
tips.assistantTemplates.title: Have the Assistant set up a team
tips.assistantToldWaiting.text: While the Assistant watches the lanes, an agent showing a permission prompt or asking you something wakes it, and it tells you which agent, its card and what it asks. It never answers for you. Its watch can follow a release card outside the lanes too.
tips.assistantToldWaiting.title: The Assistant tells you when an agent needs you
tips.assistantUndo.text: Done by the Assistant lists its changes by your message. Undo on a change puts it back, and Undo on a message puts back all of them; whatever you or an agent changed since is kept.
tips.assistantUndo.title: Undo the Assistant's changes
tips.assistantWaits.text: Ask the Assistant to let you know when an agent finishes a build or a test run: it waits without checking in, and Combwork wakes it when the agent finishes, needs you or stops.
tips.assistantWaits.title: Have the Assistant tell you when an agent is done
tips.attachFiles.text: Drop a PDF, a log or any file onto an agent's terminal: Combwork keeps a copy with the session and pastes its path. A chip shows what's attached, and says when the agent's CLI doesn't read that kind of file itself, so the agent opens it by its path.
tips.attachFiles.title: Attach any file to a prompt
tips.attachmentsTabs.text: The Attachments tab has Pane attachments and Card attachments. Show in Attachments, beside a card's attachments, opens Card attachments at that card; Show Session's Attachments, in an agent's ⋯ menu, opens Pane attachments at its session.
tips.attachmentsTabs.title: Jump to a card's or a session's files
tips.autoModeSetup.text: In auto mode, Claude Code may offer to teach auto mode about your environment. Combwork never answers it: the agent shows Needs input, and nothing is typed into it, until you do. Settings → Advanced → Claude Code can turn the offer off.
tips.autoModeSetup.title: Claude Code's offer waits for you
tips.backupRetention.text: Combwork compresses its transcript backups once a session ends, and Storage shows what they hold. To let old ones go, set Settings → Sessions → Keep transcript backups: only copies of sessions the CLI still has go to the Recycle Bin.
tips.backupRetention.title: Backups take less room, and can expire
tips.banners.text: Each thing is told once: a pop-up while you use Combwork, a Windows notification while it is in the background, and either way it is kept under the bell, with its buttons while they apply. Settings → Notifications chooses where pop-ups go.
tips.banners.title: Every notification is under the bell
tips.board.text: Cards in On Hold, Todo, Active, Review, Approved and Done, each for a project. Start… gives a card to an agent with the card as its prompt. {key}
tips.board.title: Plan work on the task board
tips.boardArchive.text: Tick Archived on the board for a table of archived cards: sort and filter them by project, label or the column they came from, and Unarchive one or a whole selection.
tips.boardArchive.title: Find an archived card
tips.boardArchiveAll.text: A column's ⋯ has Archive All in Done (n)…, and the board's ⋯ has Archive All Cards… for every column. Cards agents are on are skipped unless you say, and Undo puts everything back where it was.
tips.boardArchiveAll.title: Clear a column in one go
tips.boardDoing.text: Drag a card into Active and Combwork asks: nobody yet, an agent without starting anything, or an agent that starts on it now.
tips.boardDoing.title: Choose who works on a card in Active
tips.boardDone.text: A reviewer moves a card that passes its review to Approved; Done means merged, and an agent moves its cards there after merging its work. Say "merged, move #65 to done" and it does; the card's history shows who moved it.
tips.boardDone.title: Approved, then Done once merged
tips.boardExport.text: The board is kept in the workspace's database. Export Board to JSON… in the board's ⋯ menu saves every card as a JSON file, archived ones too, in a folder you choose.
tips.boardExport.title: Your board as plain files
tips.boardFold.text: Collapse a column to a narrow strip with the « in its header, and fold cards to one line with their ▾; a column's ⋯ collapses or expands all its cards. Combwork remembers them for the workspace.
tips.boardFold.title: Fold the board to what matters
tips.boardHygiene.text: Ask the Assistant to tidy the board: it links duplicate cards for you to archive, records your answers as decisions on their cards, and raises blocked reasons that are out of date.
tips.boardHygiene.title: Ask the Assistant to tidy the board
tips.boardOrder.text: Drag the most important cards to the top, or ask the Assistant or an agent to prioritise: they reorder the board itself.
tips.boardOrder.title: A column's order is its priority
tips.boardReview.text: Say "review #87" to another agent: the card stays in Review with the agent that did the work, shows who is reviewing it, and gets the verdict as a comment. When it passes, the reviewer moves it to Approved.
tips.boardReview.title: Have an agent review a card
tips.boardSetAside.text: Opened in an older Combwork, a workspace gets its cards set aside when this one opens it again. Review… on the notice, or Set-Aside Cards… in the board's ⋯ menu, adds each to the board or discards it.
tips.boardSetAside.title: Cards made by an older Combwork
tips.boardStages.text: The board’s columns are the stages your workflow options make: Merging sits under Approved while Combwork merges, and a stage nobody uses is hidden. Ask the Assistant to rename one, such as “call Active Building in web”: a name changes no rule.
tips.boardStages.title: The board shows your workflow’s stages
tips.boardUpgrade.text: Combwork keeps the 0.9 board it upgraded to 1.0. Help → Restore the 0.9 Board Backup… puts it back, after keeping a copy of the board as it is, so version 0.9 can change it again.
tips.boardUpgrade.title: Back to 0.9 after the upgrade
tips.branchCards.text: In Version Control → Branches & remotes, a branch a card works on shows the card and its stage, and in Review the revision under review. Click the card to open it.
tips.branchCards.title: See which card a branch is for
tips.branchCleanup.text: Version Control → Branches & remotes groups the branches as In use, Merged and Not merged. Clean Up Merged Branches… deletes the merged ones nothing uses, and offers the merged ones on your remotes apart, never ticked for you.
tips.branchCleanup.title: Clean up merged branches
tips.cardAttachments.text: Paste or drop files into a card's description or comment: they are kept with the card when you save or post, shown in it, and listed for the agent that starts it. The pin on a pane's attachment chip copies a file to the agent's card.
tips.cardAttachments.title: Keep a screenshot with its card
tips.cardAttachmentsCleanup.text: Files kept with a card go to the Recycle Bin 30 days after it is archived. Choose 3, 7 or 90 days, or Never, in Project Settings → Storage, where Clean Up Now… removes what is due at once. Open and Done cards keep theirs.
tips.cardAttachmentsCleanup.title: Archived cards' screenshots clean up after themselves
tips.cardAttachmentsFolders.text: Agents attach files to cards from their own project and the temp folder. Keep test evidence in a folder of your own? List it in Settings → Advanced → Card attachments: more folders, and they can attach from there without copying into Temp.
tips.cardAttachmentsFolders.title: Let agents attach your test evidence where it is
tips.cardCost.text: A card's panel says what its agents used while they held it, "{example}", with the builder's and reviewer's parts and tokens on hover. Performance lists every card's cost, and a lane's hover in the Progress panel its overhead.
tips.cardCost.title: What a card cost
tips.cardCostRounds.text: A card's Work section ends with its cost by round: the builder's and reviewer's parts in each round, adding up to the card's cost. See whether extra rounds or one long read drove it.
tips.cardCostRounds.title: What each review round cost
tips.cardDecisions.text: A card's Decisions, above its comments, hold what you decided: agents check their work against them before Review, and reviewers fail work that ignores one. Tell the Assistant a decision and it records it there; an agent waiting for your answer is told.
tips.cardDecisions.title: Put what you decide on the card
tips.cardLinks.text: Card numbers an agent or the Assistant prints, like #12, are links: hover one for its title and column, and Ctrl+click it to open the card.
tips.cardLinks.title: Ctrl+click a card number in the terminal
tips.cardLoop.text: Tell one agent to work through some cards as the builder and another to review them: each waits for the other at no cost, and Combwork wakes it when the card changes.
tips.cardLoop.title: Let two agents build and review in turn
tips.cardMove.text: Drag any dialog by its header (a card, Add Agent, Agent Settings…) to see what's behind it; Escape while dragging puts it back.
tips.cardMove.title: Move a dialog out of the way
tips.cardReadFirst.text: In a card's Read first, list the doc sections it needs, like docs/PLAN.md#setup: the agent's start prompt lists them, so it reads those sections instead of a whole plan. Click one to read it in Combwork.
tips.cardReadFirst.title: Point a card at the docs it needs
tips.cardSummaries.text: Agents start a card's report or review verdict with one line saying what is ready or what was found, the details below; they and the Assistant read just those lines when that's enough.
tips.cardSummaries.title: Reports start with the gist
tips.cardWork.text: Open a card: its Work section lists each revision submitted for review, with its round, files, verdicts and checks, and how it was merged. On the board, a card shows its revision and last verdict.
tips.cardWork.title: See what a card’s work went through
tips.chooseConnections.text: Project Settings → Agents → Choose Connections… picks a connection for each role of the project's agents (or one for all, or per agent), changing nothing else. Loading a template offers the same choice.
tips.chooseConnections.title: High effort for every builder, in one go
tips.claudeStatusLine.text: Combwork's status line feeds an agent's footer and shows nothing in the pane. Turn off Settings → Advanced → Combwork's status line in place of yours to see the one in your Claude Code settings again: Combwork still reads the status.
tips.claudeStatusLine.title: Keep your own Claude Code status line
tips.cliOverrides.text: Combwork changes a little of how each CLI behaves in its sessions, such as Copilot not updating itself or Codex's terminal title. Each change can be turned off in Settings → Advanced, under its CLI, which says what Combwork can no longer do without it.
tips.cliOverrides.title: Keep a CLI as it is outside Combwork
tips.cliOwnMode.text: Choose The CLI's own setting as an agent's or a project's permission mode and Combwork passes none: the CLI starts in the mode its own config sets. The badge says CLI's own, and switching a running session restarts it.
tips.cliOwnMode.title: Let the CLI's own config choose the mode
tips.closeCommands.text: Settings → Workspace → When this workspace closes, run: Combwork runs your command once it has closed the workspace and finished writing its files, and shows it running until it ends.
tips.closeCommands.title: Run a backup as a workspace closes
tips.closeWindow.text: With several windows open, File → Close Window ({key}) closes just this one, as its X does. Exit Combwork (all windows) closes every window and stops all their agents.
tips.closeWindow.title: Close one window, or all of them
tips.codexSandboxConnections.text: Codex connections keep asking for Administrator permission? Each one's admin sandbox setup resets the others'. Settings → Advanced → Codex → Connections: use Codex's non-admin sandbox runs them all without it, at the cost of separate sandbox accounts.
tips.codexSandboxConnections.title: Several Codex connections, no admin prompts
tips.codexScriptCalls.text: Codex in code mode runs its tools from a script. In the Sessions tab, a Script line says how many calls it made and which; open it to read each call with its own result.
tips.codexScriptCalls.title: See what a Codex script did
tips.combworkFolder.text: Combwork keeps each project's .combwork folder (sessions, backups, launch settings) out of git by itself. Where it can't, say with no git, another version control system, or a folder OneDrive or Dropbox syncs, the project's Overview tells you.
tips.combworkFolder.title: A project's .combwork stays on this computer
tips.combworkMerges.text: In Version Control → Workflow, choose Pair, or set Who merges to Combwork merges: Combwork’s merge queue merges each approved card once its checks pass on the merged result, so red work never reaches the target branch.
tips.combworkMerges.title: Let Combwork merge approved cards
tips.combworkSkills.text: Agents and the Assistant get Combwork's own skills: work-on-card, review-agent-work, handover and more. Combwork keeps them up to date; ones you edit stay yours.
tips.combworkSkills.title: Skills for working with Combwork
tips.compactFocus.text: Compact summarises the conversation so every later message costs less. Give it a focus ("keep the API decisions, drop the test output") and the agent keeps what matters. {key}
tips.compactFocus.title: Compact with a focus
tips.compactSidebar.text: Toggle Compact Sidebar turns the project list into a narrow rail of tiles with each project's agents, leaving more room for the terminals.
tips.compactSidebar.title: A compact project list
tips.compactionHistory.text: The Overview's compaction history pages, filters and sorts a long session's compactions; click one to read it in the transcript, with the summary the agent carried on from.
tips.compactionHistory.title: Read a compaction where it happened
tips.compareBranches.text: Version Control → Changes compares any two local branches without checking anything out: pick one under Branches to see the commits each has that the other hasn't, the files it changes, and each file's diff.
tips.compareBranches.title: Compare two branches, such as 1.0.0 with main
tips.conflictHunks.text: When the merge queue sends a card back for a conflict, its Work section lists the files: click one to see its conflicts, the target's side and the card's under their names, as the queue's test merge had them.
tips.conflictHunks.title: See a returned card's conflicts
tips.connectionOrder.text: Drag accounts into your order in Settings → Accounts & Connections: a new agent gets the first connection of the first account that's on in the workspace. Running agents keep theirs.
tips.connectionOrder.title: Put your accounts in order
tips.connectionSetups.text: Add Connection under an account in Settings → Accounts & Connections makes another setup on the same sign-in, say "Claude · High" beside "Claude · Medium". Agents choose a connection, so one edit changes every agent on it.
tips.connectionSetups.title: Several setups on one sign-in
tips.connectionTags.text: Give connections on both accounts the same tag, such as Builders or Assistant (the Tag box in a connection's dialog): when a usage move sends agents to the other account, each goes to the connection with its tag, and the Assistant moves too.
tips.connectionTags.title: Tag connections so moved agents keep their kind
tips.connectionTrust.text: A new connection's Set Up asks Claude Code once, in the workspace folder, to trust every project in it. Codex agents never ask: each trusts its own folder for that launch (Settings → Advanced → Codex).
tips.connectionTrust.title: Trust a workspace in one answer
tips.connections.text: Settings → Accounts & Connections keeps several Claude Code and Codex sign-ins, or a server such as Ollama on this PC. Each workspace chooses which accounts are on, and each agent runs on the connection it chose: pick another in Agent Settings.
tips.connections.title: Run agents on different sign-ins
tips.consoleRecording.text: In the developer console, Record writes what an agent's CLI sends Combwork to a file, redacted unless you tick text for that recording, and Copy Diagnostics can attach it to a bug report.
tips.consoleRecording.title: Record what a CLI sends
tips.consoleText.text: Settings → Advanced → Developer console: show prompt, reply and command text shows them in the developer console, under a banner saying so, and ticks text for new recordings. Tokens and sign-ins stay masked, and agents' cw_console stays redacted.
tips.consoleText.title: See the text in the developer console
tips.copilot.text: Agents can use the GitHub Copilot CLI, Copilot Free included. Provider Setup installs it and says who it is signed in as: its own login or the GitHub CLI’s.
tips.copilot.title: Run agents on GitHub Copilot
tips.copilotModes.text: Copilot agents start in Accept edits: they edit files in their own folder and use the Combwork tools without asking, and ask before other commands, other MCP tools and web access. Choose Ask to approve each edit too, or Allow all to approve everything.
tips.copilotModes.title: What Copilot agents ask before
tips.copyDiagnostics.text: Help → Copy Diagnostics… gathers Combwork's version, your coding agents, key settings and the end of the log for a bug report, with names, folders and tokens taken out.
tips.copyDiagnostics.title: Found a bug? Copy Diagnostics
tips.ctrlCvToCli.text: In an agent's pane Ctrl+C copies a selection and Ctrl+V pastes. Turn on Settings → Advanced → Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V go to the CLI to send both keys to the CLI instead, as in any other terminal; right-click still copies and pastes.
tips.ctrlCvToCli.title: Give Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V to the agent's CLI
tips.customCommands.text: Name a command once in Settings → Commands and run it from the command palette (Run Command), or pick it for when a workspace opens or closes: a local server or a database your agents need, say. As a workspace opens, its agents start once they are done.
tips.customCommands.title: Your own commands, one click away
tips.dateFormat.text: Combwork shows dates as {date} and times as {time}. Settings → General → Date format and Time format change them everywhere, sessions named by when they started too.
tips.dateFormat.title: Dates your way
tips.designCheck.text: Ask a card loop’s builder for a design first: it posts it on the card, Combwork wakes the reviewer to check it, and the answer wakes the builder. With no answer within the Design check wait (Version Control → Workflow → Card loops), it goes ahead as posted.
tips.designCheck.title: Have a design checked before the build
tips.developerConsole.text: Turn on Settings → Advanced → Show developer features, then Help → Developer Console opens a window of its own: pick an agent and see each hook and status line beside what Combwork made of it, redacted. Filter, search and pause as it runs.
tips.developerConsole.title: Watch what a CLI sends Combwork
tips.dialects.text: The Dialects view shows every text Combwork gives agents, and lets a model, a CLI or the workspace word some of them its own way. Duplicate a file to try a change on one agent (Agent Settings → Dialect); it applies at the agent's next launch.
tips.dialects.title: Tune the words Combwork gives agents
tips.dialectsNewModel.text: In the Dialects view, New Model File on a CLI's group starts a file for a model, even one no agent runs yet: type its ID. Duplicate can name the copy's model too, and Set Model gives one of your files to a model. It applies at each agent's next launch.
tips.dialectsNewModel.title: A dialect file for any model
tips.editTemplates.text: Select a template in the Templates view and choose Edit…: add, copy, reorder or remove its agents, change each in the Agent Settings dialog (its Save saves the template too), rename it and pick its layout.
tips.editTemplates.title: Edit a template in place
tips.fileLinks.text: File paths an agent prints, like src/app.ts:42, are links: Ctrl+click one to open the file in the Files tab at that line.
tips.fileLinks.title: Ctrl+click a path in the terminal
tips.filesTab.text: The Files tab browses and edits the project, previews Markdown, CSV, HTML and images, and keeps unsaved edits as you switch.
tips.filesTab.title: Edit files without leaving Combwork
tips.flightRecorder.text: Turn on a flight recorder trigger in Settings → Advanced (safeguard stops, something unknown from a CLI, a CLI version change, an agent gone silent), and Combwork saves the agent's recent developer console events, redacted, when it happens, with a notice.
tips.flightRecorder.title: Catch rare events by themselves
tips.focusedTests.text: With Combwork merging, Version Control → Workflow can run each card’s focused tests on the merged result: your project’s command chooses the tests a change needs when the card is submitted, and the merge queue runs them before it merges.
tips.focusedTests.title: Each card’s own tests before it merges
tips.followUpCheck.text: When you ask for a change to a card in Review or Approved for its reviewer to check, its builder posts the change as a follow-up: Combwork wakes the reviewer, and the answer wakes the builder. One left unanswered for 15 minutes shows its card as stalled.
tips.followUpCheck.title: Have a follow-up checked without a new round
tips.forYou.text: A card with a For you chip waits for you: an approval, a decision or a question. The Task Board icon counts them, and For you on the board shows only those. Open the card to approve, decline or answer: the agent waiting on it hears at once.
tips.forYou.title: Answer what waits for you
tips.forYouActions.text: When an agent's question is about something only you can do on its card, it can offer it as a button under the question: Move to Done, Make It No Code or Unblock, with its suggested reason, which you can change. One click does it and answers the agent.
tips.forYouActions.title: Answer with one click
tips.forYouApproveNote.text: Approve takes an optional note. On an agent's question it's recorded as your decision on the card, so the agent works to it and its reviewer checks it; on Combwork's own requests it's your comment. Left empty, Approve is one click.
tips.forYouApproveNote.title: Approve, but change something
tips.generalistRole.text: Give an agent the Generalist role in the workflow (Agent Settings) and it does whatever you ask in its pane: it is never put in a lane or asked to review. A card it takes still follows the project’s workflow.
tips.generalistRole.title: An agent for whatever you ask
tips.gitCheck.text: Help → Provider Setup… shows the git Combwork found and its version. Worktree agents, merging and the Version Control tab’s Git sections need Git for Windows 2.38 or later.
tips.gitCheck.title: Is git ready for worktrees?
tips.gitHistory.text: Version Control → History opens on the branch your work merges into. Pick another in its heading, yours or a remote’s, and page back through older commits under the list.
tips.gitHistory.title: See the history of any branch
tips.gitInit.text: A project without git? Its Version Control tab's Initialise repository… makes it one on main, keeps .combwork out, adds a starter .gitignore if you like and makes the first commit, so agents can work in worktrees at once.
tips.gitInit.title: Make a project a git repository in one click
tips.gitRemotes.text: Version Control → Branches & remotes: Push to… sends this branch, or every branch and tag, to any remote without changing what the branch tracks. A remote can be renamed or removed there, and a branch's Track… chooses what Pull and Push use.
tips.gitRemotes.title: Push to a backup remote
tips.gitView.text: In a Git project, the Version Control tab shows its branch, remotes, history and tags, and lets you switch or create a branch, fetch, pull, push, tag and set its commit identity. The status bar shows "{example}": click it to get there.
tips.gitView.title: See and change a project's git
tips.gotoProject.text: Press {key} and type a few letters of its name.
tips.gotoProject.title: Jump to a project
tips.handoverSelf.text: When an agent's transcript size turns amber, click it and choose the agent itself: it writes a handover, and a new conversation picks up from it, short and fast again.
tips.handoverSelf.title: A long conversation? Hand it over to itself
tips.hardwareAcceleration.text: If your graphics driver leaves Combwork's window blank, flickering or crashing, turn on Settings → Advanced → Disable hardware acceleration and restart Combwork. A window that doesn't draw at all: start Combwork once with --disable-gpu.
tips.hardwareAcceleration.title: A blank or flickering window?
tips.hooksMissing.text: If a CLI update or a policy stops an agent’s hooks reaching Combwork, its pane says Status unknown instead of a status that may be wrong, nothing is typed into it and its lane pauses. The banner over its pane says why when Combwork can tell.
tips.hooksMissing.title: When an agent’s hooks stop arriving
tips.howDoYouWork.text: A new project’s Version Control tab asks “How do you work?”: Solo, Pair or Team, the one that fits its agents suggested. Choose sets it up in one click; Not Now keeps your defaults.
tips.howDoYouWork.title: Start a new project with a preset
tips.imagesTab.text: The Attachments tab keeps each screenshot and file pasted or dropped into the project's sessions, grouped by session, with previews and a filter by kind, ready to insert again.
tips.imagesTab.title: Everything you attached, in one place
tips.improveTranslation.text: Spotted a clumsy or wrong word in your language? Help → Improve This Translation shows how to fix it, or add a language, with a pull request on GitHub.
tips.improveTranslation.title: Make Combwork read better in your language
tips.inboxCarryingOn.text: Combwork tells a working agent of new messages at a tool's end, keeps it going to read them before it stops, and wakes it when idle. Each has a switch in Settings → Advanced, and a project can set its own; with wakes off, the pane's Deliver Now types the line.
tips.inboxCarryingOn.title: Choose how agents hear of their inbox
tips.inboxNotices.text: A message the Assistant leaves a working agent reaches it at its next tool call, or before its turn ends, as a short notice from Combwork: nothing is typed over its work. The agent reads and acks it in its inbox; its pane shows it as unread (✉) until it does.
tips.inboxNotices.title: Messages reach a busy agent between steps
tips.isolatedChecks.text: In a shared folder, another agent's edit during a check makes it not count. cw-progress --check typecheck --isolated runs it in a copy of its own at the card's revision, which nothing else writes. Stop in the Progress panel ends it and all it started.
tips.isolatedChecks.title: A check nobody else can spoil
tips.keepAwake.text: While an agent works, Combwork stops Windows from sleeping (the screen can still lock), and lets it sleep once they're done. Choose when in Settings → General.
tips.keepAwake.title: Leave agents working, the PC stays awake
tips.laneApplyNow.text: In Start Lane for a lane's builder, Apply now changes the order at once: the card being worked goes back to Todo with its work kept on its branch, and the builder is told.
tips.laneApplyNow.title: Reorder a running lane now
tips.laneBranchSquash.text: After an agent's card is squash-merged, Combwork brings its branch up to date before its next card, so each review shows only that card's work. What it can't do safely it asks under For you; Settings → Advanced makes it ask every time.
tips.laneBranchSquash.title: An agent's branch kept up to date between cards
tips.laneGates.text: In the Progress panel, a lane says why it waits in its header, and a red notch on a card’s segment means its last request was refused: hover it for why and what next.
tips.laneGates.title: See why a lane isn’t moving
tips.laneNext.text: With workflow rules on, once a lane's card is Done Combwork gives the next one to its builder as soon as the builder's turn is over, so the lane goes on without a prompt from you or the Assistant.
tips.laneNext.title: Combwork starts a lane's next card
tips.laneNotices.text: Combwork notifies you when a lane's review fails, a card is blocked or stalls, or every card has passed so its merge is due, one notice per lane. Settings → Notifications decides where they appear.
tips.laneNotices.title: Hear how a lane goes, without the Assistant
tips.laneSlots.text: In the Progress panel, a lane names its slot after its agents (· slot-b): point at it for the branch being built there and whether the slot is ready, or click it for Branches & remotes.
tips.laneSlots.title: See where a lane builds
tips.laneStart.text: Right-click the Todo column and choose Start Lane with These Cards…: pick the builder and the reviewer, put the cards in order, and both start with a brief. End or abandon a lane from its row in the Progress panel.
tips.laneStart.title: Start a lane yourself
tips.lanesLegend.text: Hover over the Lanes bar in the Progress panel for its legend: each colour is a category, with the stages in it. A lane marked old rules keeps the workflow options it started with until it ends.
tips.lanesLegend.title: What a lane’s colours mean
tips.language.text: Combwork follows Windows' display language when it has it. Settings → General → Language picks another; languages translated by AI are marked, and improvements are welcome. Agents are still spoken to in English.
tips.language.title: Combwork in your language
tips.leftRunning.text: A process an agent's command started that keeps running after its shell has gone shows in Activity as Left running, with its CPU time and End It. Past ten minutes, a notice says so once, and the agent is told too.
tips.leftRunning.title: Spot what a command left running
tips.leftoverBranches.text: Version Control → Changes lists leftover branches: a superseded or archived card’s, an agent’s from before slots. Compare one with your target first, then Delete… it; one with commits of its own lists them before it goes.
tips.leftoverBranches.title: Clean up branches nothing uses
tips.leftoverProcesses.text: A preview server or a tail -f an agent started can keep running after it stops, holding the project's folder or a port. Combwork lists them in the ⋯ menu on the agent's pane and offers to end them; Settings → Agents can end them every time.
tips.leftoverProcesses.title: End what a stopped agent left running
tips.licenceAudit.text: Before a release, ask an agent to audit the licences of what your project ships. It reads them from the files, vendored material and installer parts included, and flags anything unclear for you.
tips.licenceAudit.title: Audit the licences of what you ship
tips.loopDefaults.text: Rounds and Wait under Card loops in Settings → Version Control set what loops use when you don't say ({rounds, plural, one {# round} other {# rounds}} and {hours, plural, one {# hour} other {# hours}} to start with); a workspace and a project can set their own. Saying "rounds: 3" when you start one still wins.
tips.loopDefaults.title: Your rounds and wait for every loop
tips.loopLanes.text: When two agents build and review cards in turn, Combwork keeps the loop as a lane: its cards in order, the one it's on, and whether it's paused on a blocked card. Ask the Assistant which lanes are running.
tips.loopLanes.title: Combwork keeps your card loops as lanes
tips.loopWakes.text: When a card arrives in Review, Combwork wakes its reviewer, and on the verdict its builder, even if one forgot to wait. To drive reviews by hand, turn off Wake reviewers and builders in the project's Version Control → Workflow → Card loops.
tips.loopWakes.title: Loops keep going on their own
tips.mainProcessStalls.text: Typing lagged a moment? Performance → Main process stalls lists the times Combwork's main process was busy since it started: how long, whether it was working or waiting, and what was under way.
tips.mainProcessStalls.title: See why Combwork felt slow
tips.maxAgents.text: Maximum agents in Version Control → Workflow is how many agents a project has, so nobody brings in agents you didn’t plan for, the Assistant included. Each preset sets its team: Solo one agent, Pair a builder and a reviewer. Raise it there to add more.
tips.maxAgents.title: Your team size
tips.mcpCatalogue.text: The MCP view's Catalogue lists servers you can install, Combwork's own first. Each download is checked against its catalogue and shows what it runs; updates are offered, never automatic. Add a company's catalogue in Settings → MCP Catalogues.
tips.mcpCatalogue.title: Install a server from a catalogue
tips.mcpFromFile.textAdded: Got a server as a .json definition or a .zip of its folder? Add MCP Server from File in the MCP view shows what it runs and adds it to the workspace: then add it to the projects that need it, with Add to… or in their MCP tab.
tips.mcpFromFile.title: Add an MCP server from a file
tips.mcpPerAgent.text: In an agent's settings, MCP servers: Only these gives it just the servers it needs, such as a sandbox server for a release tester, and keeps the others' tools out of its context.
tips.mcpPerAgent.title: MCP servers for some agents only
tips.mcpPerProject.textAdded: A workspace MCP server runs only where it is added: Add Server… in a project's MCP tab picks one, showing what it runs. Its tools stay out of the other projects' agents' context, and the tab lists only what that project uses.
tips.mcpPerProject.title: MCP servers only where they are needed
tips.mcpSearch.text: The MCP view and Add Server… search your servers by name, description and tags (a definition's "tags" list), and show those added somewhere or nowhere.
tips.mcpSearch.title: Find a server in a long list
tips.memorySnapshot.text: Turn on Settings → Advanced → Save a memory snapshot if Combwork is about to run out of memory, to find out what filled it. Snapshots can be gigabytes, hold what Combwork had in memory (card text, transcripts, possibly tokens) and stay on this PC.
tips.memorySnapshot.title: Combwork closed running out of memory?
tips.mergeBranch.text: ⑂ beside a branch in Version Control → Branches & remotes merges it into the branch you pick, one merge at a time. A card's branch that isn't Done asks first, and the card is marked merged outside the rules.
tips.mergeBranch.title: Merge a branch by hand
tips.mergeMessage.text: With Combwork merging, Version Control → Workflow sets the merge’s commit message: Combwork’s names the card, the branch’s own keeps card keys out of your history. With Squash, each card then lands as one commit with its builder’s message.
tips.mergeMessage.title: Merges with your own commit messages
tips.mergePush.text: With Combwork merging, Version Control → Workflow can push the target branch after each merge, never forced. If the remote refuses it, the queue pauses and says why: pull and resume, or turn it off and resume.
tips.mergePush.title: Push each merge to your remote
tips.mergeQueueFolder.text: When the merge queue merges into a branch checked out in a folder (main in the project folder), it updates the folder too, but pauses rather than touch a file you are changing. Settings → Advanced can have it ask you under For you first.
tips.mergeQueueFolder.title: Merging into the folder you work in
tips.mergeQueuePanel.text: The Progress panel's Merges tab shows each merge queue: the card it is testing and how long its checks usually take, the cards waiting, and a card it returned until you've seen it. Pause queue and Resume queue are there too.
tips.mergeQueuePanel.title: Watch the merge queue
tips.mergeQueueRecent.text: Under each merge queue in the Progress panel's Merges tab, Recent merges lists its latest merges, returns and pauses, with why, when and how long each took. Click one to open its card.
tips.mergeQueueRecent.title: See what the merge queue did lately
tips.mergeRebase.text: With Combwork merging, set Merge style to Rebase and fast-forward in Version Control → Workflow: the merge queue rebases each card onto the target, tests exactly that, and moves the target forward to it.
tips.mergeRebase.title: A linear history, with no merge commits
tips.mergeSlot.text: When several agents finish at once, each claims the project's merge slot before it merges main in, checks and merges, so nobody's checks have to run twice. Who holds it and who waits shows in the Overview and the Progress panel.
tips.mergeSlot.title: Agents take turns to merge
tips.mergeStrict.text: With Combwork merging, Version Control → Workflow can have work up to date with its target before it merges: the merge queue updates a card in its own folder, never on the builder’s branch, and the review still counts if it’s the same change.
tips.mergeStrict.title: Work up to date before it merges
tips.messageReceipts.text: Every message the Assistant leaves an agent has an id and is kept, even across a restart: it is received once the agent reads its inbox, and acked once the agent acted on it. One not acked within {minutes, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}} shows as overdue (✉) in its pane.
tips.messageReceipts.title: See where a message got to
tips.modelFallbacks.text: Combwork asks Claude Code and Codex which models they have and which effort levels each takes. If a CLI can't say, the model, effort and price lists on its Settings page are yours to edit.
tips.modelFallbacks.title: New models without a Combwork update
tips.modelSwitched.text: If an agent ends up on another model than its connection gave it (Codex's offer of a cheaper model near your limit, or /model), its footer marks the model with a warning and Activity says Model changed. Restart the agent to go back.
tips.modelSwitched.title: An agent on another model is marked
tips.modes.text: Coordinator runs the agents, Planner shapes work, QA triager turns reports into cards, Release manager takes a release through its checklist. Switch mode from the panel at once, keeping the conversation, or write your own.
tips.modes.title: Modes for the Assistant
tips.moreAgents.text: Need more than {usual, plural, one {# agent} other {# agents}} in a project? Raise Maximum agents in Version Control → Workflow, up to {most, number}, then add them. Above {usual, number} it shows what they cost: the memory your running agents take, and how much is free.
tips.moreAgents.title: More than {usual, plural, one {# agent} other {# agents}}
tips.moveAnyway.text: Dragging a card past a rule of its project (to Done before its review, say) asks first and names the rules it skips. Move Anyway records an override on the card, with your reason: an open lock on its tile says who, which rules and why.
tips.moveAnyway.title: Move a card past its rules, with a reason
tips.myPrices.text: Claude Code's cost is its own figure, from its price table. On other rates (a discount, another tier)? Set Session costs to My prices, and Combwork prices every session from your table instead.
tips.myPrices.title: Your own prices for Claude Code
tips.newCard.text: Press {key} for a new card for the project you are in, without leaving what you are doing.
tips.newCard.title: Jot down a card
tips.noCodeCards.text: A decision, a write-up or a trial has nothing to commit: tick No code in the New Card dialog. Its work is submitted with a summary and goes to Done with nothing to merge.
tips.noCodeCards.title: Cards with no code
tips.off.message: Help → Tips… still has them, and Settings → General turns them back on.
tips.off.title: Tips are off
tips.oneAgent.text: The ▾ beside Resume (n) and Stop (n) in the project header lists those agents: choose one to act on it alone. Agents ▾ and a project's right-click menu have the same for Start New, Archive and Start New, Resume All and Stop All.
tips.oneAgent.title: Resume or stop just one agent
tips.outageResume.text: Turn on Settings → Advanced → Resume agents after a connection drops, and an agent stopped by a router restart or a Wi-Fi blip waits for the connection, then reruns what was cut off by itself. Never for a usage limit or an expired sign-in.
tips.outageResume.title: Agents can carry on after a connection drops
tips.overview.text: The Workspace Overview shows what every project used, what runs now and the board, by day. {key}
tips.overview.title: The whole workspace at a glance
tips.ownShortcuts.text: Settings → Keyboard Shortcuts changes any shortcut, and Project Settings can change them for one project.
tips.ownShortcuts.title: Make the shortcuts yours
tips.palette.text: Press {key} and type: every command, with its shortcut.
tips.palette.title: Everything is in the command palette
tips.paneCells.text: Drag a pane by its header onto an empty pane to move it there, or onto another to swap them. Each layout keeps where you put them, so switching layouts and back restores it.
tips.paneCells.title: Put an agent in any pane
tips.pasteScreenshot.text: Press Ctrl+V in an agent's terminal with an image on the clipboard, or drop an image onto it: the agent sees it, and Combwork keeps a copy.
tips.pasteScreenshot.title: Paste a screenshot into a session
tips.pathsLeftOut.text: Without version control, a card's work is only the files its paths list. When you drag one to Review and other files changed since it started, Combwork lists them first: include them in its work, or leave them out.
tips.pathsLeftOut.title: No version control? Check what a card covers
tips.pauseTeam.text: Pause the Team, in the Progress panel's Lanes, stops lanes starting cards and agents being woken, tells each agent to park, and lists what still runs until it's safe to install: then Install Now.
tips.pauseTeam.title: Pause the team before an update
tips.perfCompare.text: Performance → Compare: keep the current view before a change and again after it, and see whether Combwork’s traffic fell while the work still got done.
tips.perfCompare.title: Before and after a change
tips.perfCompareAgents.text: Comparing two scenario benchmarks? Open a scenario in Performance → Compare: its measures show the session under test first, then the other agents (a lane’s builder and reviewer) and all of them together, with each agent’s Combwork tool calls.
tips.perfCompareAgents.title: Which agent a change came from
tips.performance.text: Performance, in the activity bar, shows what Combwork's API, tools and guidance cost for the last day, week or month: the whole workspace or one project. Each project has its own Performance tab too.
tips.performance.title: What Combwork itself costs
tips.permissionMode.text: Click the mode in an agent's footer, or press {key}, to move between asking first, accepting edits and planning.
tips.permissionMode.title: Switch permission mode
tips.progressCard.text: A run in the Progress panel shows the card and the revision it ran on under the agent, such as #1061 · a3f2c1d: click the card to open it, or the revision to copy it.
tips.progressCard.title: Which card was that run for?
tips.progressCheck.text: A run for a card is recorded as a check of the card's revision. Its details in the Progress panel say Counts as check, or why not: it wasn't started as the check, the folder had uncommitted changes, or files changed while it ran.
tips.progressCheck.title: Did that run count as a check?
tips.progressCommand.text: Agents run long commands such as tests and builds through cw-progress, so the Progress panel shows them under the agent's name, with about how long is left from the second time. Settings can have them do it only when you ask.
tips.progressCommand.title: Progress for any command
tips.progressDetails.text: Click a run in the Progress panel, or one under Recent, for its details: the whole command, when it ran and how long it took, its exit code, the log it wrote and why it failed.
tips.progressDetails.title: What did that run do?
tips.progressFilter.text: When several projects run tests and builds, the dropdown at the top of the Progress panel shows just one project's runs, or one agent's. Each workspace remembers the choice.
tips.progressFilter.title: Only one project's runs
tips.progressHistory.text: The Runs tab of the Progress panel keeps the last {kept, plural, one {# run} other {# runs}}, even after Combwork restarts: by day, a run and its retries in one line. Find them by their words, or show only failures, a lane’s or an agent’s.
tips.progressHistory.title: What ran this morning?
tips.progressLanes.text: When pairs of agents work through cards, the bottom of the Progress panel shows each lane as a bar, a segment per card coloured by where it is. Hover one for its card and round; click to open it. A merge going on shows as a teal card at the top.
tips.progressLanes.title: How far along is each pair?
tips.progressLanesHeight.text: The Progress panel shows up to four lanes. Drag the line above Lanes up to see more, a whole lane at a time; double-click it to go back to four. Each workspace remembers it.
tips.progressLanesHeight.title: See more lanes at once
tips.progressLanesOrder.text: Drag a running lane up or down in the Progress panel, or focus it and press Alt+Up or Alt+Down. Each workspace keeps your order; a new lane comes in on top, and merged ones drop to the bottom.
tips.progressLanesOrder.title: Put your lanes in order
tips.progressPanel.text: When agents run tests or builds that report progress, the Progress panel on the right shows each run: the agent, how far along it is and the time left, and Combwork's taskbar button fills as they go. {key} shows it.
tips.progressPanel.title: How long until the tests finish?
tips.progressTabs.text: The Progress panel has four tabs: Pulse for what is going on now, then Merges, Runs and Lanes. A red number on Runs counts the runs that failed with nothing passing since; Pulse has a line for them too.
tips.progressTabs.title: Pulse, Merges, Runs, Lanes
tips.projectCards.text: A project's Overview starts with its cards: how many are in each column, stalled or blocked. Click a number to open its Tasks tab.
tips.projectCards.title: A project's cards at a glance
tips.projectKeys.text: Each project has a key of 2 to 4 letters that names its cards: AM-12. Search the board or the command palette for AM-12, or AM- for all of that project’s cards; an old #12 still works. Change a key in Project Settings.
tips.projectKeys.title: Cards are named by their project’s key
tips.projectTabs.text: When space is short, a project's tabs shrink to icons, and the tab you're on keeps its name while it fits. Hover a tab for its name and shortcut.
tips.projectTabs.title: Tabs that make room
tips.projectTabsKeys.text: Alt+1 to Alt+8 open a project's tabs in the order they show, Session to Git. Memory, Skills, Templates and MCP are in More ▾ at the end, and in the menu bar's Project menu.
tips.projectTabsKeys.title: Alt and a number for each tab
tips.projectTabsSettings.text: The last item of More ▾, at the end of a project's tabs, is Project Settings…, with its shortcut (Alt+0 unless you change it).
tips.projectTabsSettings.title: Project Settings from More ▾
tips.quitWhenDone.text: Quitting while an agent works offers Quit when agents finish: Combwork hides and quits by itself once they're done. Conversations are always kept.
tips.quitWhenDone.title: Quit when agents finish
tips.recentWorkspaces.text: Remove a workspace from File → Open Recent or the welcome page with its ✕, or right-click it. Clear Recently Opened forgets them all; folders that are gone show as not found.
tips.recentWorkspaces.title: Tidy your recent workspaces
tips.removeAll.text: Remove All in the project header removes all of a project's agents after one question. Worktrees are kept unless you tick the box, which deletes only merged, clean ones.
tips.removeAll.title: Remove every agent at once
tips.resumeAfterUpdate.text: Installing a new version tells the agents that were working or in a card loop, and when Combwork restarts it resumes them in their conversations, one at a time, each told its card, round and lane. After you quit, the next start offers to resume them instead.
tips.resumeAfterUpdate.title: Updates leave your agents where they were
tips.resumeAll.text: After a restart, Resume All Agents in the project header resumes every stopped agent's last session in one go.
tips.resumeAll.title: Resume all agents at once
tips.retryWait.text: When a Codex, Claude Code or Copilot agent's requests are refused, often by a rate limit, it waits and tries again while its screen says only Working. Combwork reads the wait from the agent's own records, and its status says so.
tips.retryWait.title: See when an agent is rate-limited
tips.reviewCopies.text: A reviewer reviews in a review copy: a folder at exactly the submitted revision, which nothing else writes, so the builder can carry on meanwhile. Its checks there count for that submission. Settings → Advanced turns it off.
tips.reviewCopies.title: Reviewers test exactly what was submitted
tips.reviewSkip.text: Building an installer or a quick trial needs no reviewer? Tick Skip review in the New Card dialog: submitting the card finishes it, and a code card still goes on to its merge, with its merge checks.
tips.reviewSkip.title: Cards that don't need a review
tips.reviewerPool.text: With the workflow option Reviewers set to A shared pool, Start Lane offers the reviewer pool: each card submitted goes to the next free reviewer, oldest first, never to its own builder.
tips.reviewerPool.title: Share reviewers between lanes
tips.safeguardStops.text: A shield beside an agent's status means its CLI's safety classifier stopped a response: hover it for when, the model, and the agent's last tool calls before it. Orange means its model changed since, or it waits on you.
tips.safeguardStops.title: See when a safety classifier stops an agent
tips.saveTemplate.text: Set agents up once and reuse them: + Add ▾ → Templates → Save Template… in the session toolbar keeps their settings, roles and layout, and the same menu loads them into any project.
tips.saveTemplate.title: Save your agents as a template
tips.searchClear.text: Every search and filter box has an × while it has text: click it, or press Escape, to see everything again. In a dialog or the palette, the next Escape closes it.
tips.searchClear.title: Clear a search in one go
tips.searchTranscripts.text: The Sessions tab searches every session's name, date and transcript (Ctrl+F there): the tree keeps what matches, and a hit opens the conversation at that message.
tips.searchTranscripts.title: Search every past session
tips.sessionCleanup.text: The Sessions tab's Clean Up Old Sessions… button archives or deletes every session last active more than {hours, plural, one {# hour} other {# hours}}, {week, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} or {month, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} ago. Running sessions and the one you're reading are left alone.
tips.sessionCleanup.title: Clear out old sessions
tips.sessionSizes.text: The Sessions tab shows each session's transcript size. One in amber is past Warn when a transcript is over: hand its work over to a new conversation to keep things quick.
tips.sessionSizes.title: Spot the conversations that grew too long
tips.sessionToolbar.text: The chip above the panes counts your agents by state; its ▾ lists them, most urgent first: choose one to go to it. Panes | Tiles beside it switches between the agents' terminals and a small tile each.
tips.sessionToolbar.title: Jump to any agent, or see them all as tiles
tips.sessionTree.text: In the Sessions tab, right-click a provider, an agent or a session with sub-sessions to archive or delete everything in it at once. Running sessions and ones in use are skipped, and Combwork says which.
tips.sessionTree.title: Clear out a whole branch of sessions
tips.shareTemplates.text: The Templates view (activity bar) and a project's Templates tab list every template. Export… saves one as a file for teammates; Import… brings one in, for the workspace or a project.
tips.shareTemplates.title: Share agent templates
tips.sharedNotes.text: Shared notes and handovers live in the workspace, so every project's agents can read them with Combwork's tools.
tips.sharedNotes.title: Notes every project shares
tips.signInExpired.text: If Claude Code's or Codex's sign-in expires, its agents show Needs sign-in (a violet dot) and you're told once. Sign in again, then Resume All Agents in the project header carries on the ones that stopped.
tips.signInExpired.title: When a sign-in expires
tips.silentUnknown.text: Combwork never guesses an agent is idle: when its turn has been silent for a while with no sign of its end, its pane says so. If its terminal waits at its prompt, Mark idle puts it right.
tips.silentUnknown.title: An agent silent with its state unknown
tips.skillFiles.text: Agents read a skill's SKILL.md whenever they use it, and a file it links only when they need that part. A skill's page shows each of its files in a tab, to read and edit; a link to one opens its tab.
tips.skillFiles.title: A skill can link files beside its SKILL.md
tips.skillsDelivered.text: The switch beside each Combwork skill, in the Skills view or a project's Skills tab, says whether agents get it (Delivered to agents). Copies Combwork puts in a folder for Codex and Copilot are removed once no agent works there, as Settings → Advanced says.
tips.skillsDelivered.title: Choose which skills agents get
tips.slotHeld.text: When Combwork can't tell that everything an agent's session started in a slot has ended, it keeps the slot for it rather than guess. Release Slot… in the agent's ⋯ menu shows what Combwork knows, ends what it lists if you want, and frees the slot.
tips.slotHeld.title: Free a slot held after Combwork closed
tips.slotOptions.text: Version Control → Workflow → Slots and copies holds the script run in a new slot, the files copied into it and the slots in use, and how many review copies the project keeps. They save as you change them.
tips.slotOptions.title: Set up slots in Version Control
tips.slotResume.text: A builder's conversation stays in its card's slot. Once the card ends, Resume All leaves it so the slot stays free for new work; its own Resume takes the slot back while nothing else has used it.
tips.slotResume.title: A conversation resumes where it was made
tips.slots.text: With Where cards are built set to Each card in its own folder, starting a card lends its builder a slot, a ready worktree, and makes the card's branch there. A lane keeps its slot from card to card; with every slot in use, it waits for one.
tips.slots.title: Each card on a branch of its own
tips.slotsAdopted.text: Since the upgrade, each builder's own worktree is a slot kept for it until its next card or lane takes it over. Release Slot… in the agent's ⋯ menu gives one up; once free, Combwork renames its folder to a slot name, taking its conversations with it.
tips.slotsAdopted.title: Your agents' worktrees are slots now
tips.sortTables.text: Click a column's header in Combwork's tables (shortcuts, Performance, Storage, the Overviews) to sort by it, again for the other way. Combwork remembers each table's sort and rows per page.
tips.sortTables.title: Sort any table
tips.staleMessages.text: When the Assistant relays something about a card's current round, it ties the message to that card: if the card passes or starts another round before the agent reads it, Combwork drops it as stale, so no agent reopens a passed card for an old finding.
tips.staleMessages.title: A message about a round goes stale, not late
tips.startFreshIdle.text: Long conversations cost more. Start Fresh (Idle Agents) in the project header's Agents menu gives every idle agent a new one in one step, and Combwork suggests it when a project's work has finished.
tips.startFreshIdle.title: Start idle agents fresh when work is done
tips.startNewAll.text: Start New in the project header's Agents menu gives every agent a new session after one question; Archive and Start New archives their old ones first. Their conversations stay in the Sessions tab.
tips.startNewAll.title: Fresh sessions for every agent
tips.stoppedPane.text: When an agent's session ends, its pane is dimmed and its bar says when and why (stopped by you, its lane ended, its CLI exited…). Its last output stays readable, and Resume or New Session there starts it again.
tips.stoppedPane.title: A stopped agent looks stopped
tips.storageCleanup.text: Project Settings → Storage shows how much space a project's backups, archive, attachments and worktrees take. Clean Up… moves old attachments and backups to the Recycle Bin, and shows you exactly what goes first.
tips.storageCleanup.title: See what Combwork keeps, and clean up
tips.storagePurge.text: Purge… in Project Settings → Storage, or Purge Combwork's Files… on a session, removes everything Combwork keeps for sessions: backups, attachments and leftovers. It lists every file first; the coding agents' own files and your usage totals stay.
tips.storagePurge.title: Purge what Combwork keeps
tips.taskbarBadge.text: Combwork's taskbar button shows how many agents need you, and flashes when one asks you something while Combwork is in the background.
tips.taskbarBadge.title: Glance at the taskbar
tips.teamPreset.text: Team, in Version Control → Workflow, is Pair with stricter checks: the unit tests pass before review and on the merged result, dependencies are installed from scratch before every merge, and cards labelled ui or release wait for your OK.
tips.teamPreset.title: Several builders? Try the Team preset
tips.teamTemplates.text: The Templates view’s Combwork group has ready-made teams: Solo, Pair, Pair: one provider, Team 3×3, Team 6×6 and Team 6 + pool, with builders and reviewers paired. Loading one offers to switch the project to the preset it suits.
tips.teamTemplates.title: Start from one of Combwork’s templates
tips.templateNames.text: Agent names are unique across the workspace. Loading a template from another project, give its agents new names in the list beside the template's own: Load template waits until none is taken.
tips.templateNames.title: Name a template's agents as you load it
tips.templateWorkflow.text: Save Template… can keep the project's workflow too: its rules, never its branch or commands. Loading it shows what changes, then opens Version Control → Workflow filled in, to save there.
tips.templateWorkflow.title: Keep your workflow in a template
tips.testedClis.text: Claude Code, Codex and Copilot update on their own. Provider Setup shows the version this Combwork release was tested with next to the one you have, and says when yours is newer or older.
tips.testedClis.title: See which CLI versions Combwork was tested with
tips.tileStrip.text: In an agent's focus view (Tiles), the strip on the left shows each agent's card as a small chip, tinted with the colour of the board column it is in; click one to open the card. Drag the strip's edge to make it wider, and double-click the edge to reset it.
tips.tileStrip.title: Each agent's card, beside its name
tips.tileStripOrder.text: In an agent's focus view (Tiles), drag an agent up or down the strip on the left, or press Alt+Up or Alt+Down on it. The tiles and the panes follow the same order.
tips.tileStripOrder.title: Reorder agents from the focus view
tips.tilesView.text: Tiles shows each agent as a small tile: its state, status, card, progress and latest reply, twelve to a page. Click one to open its pane large beside the others; Esc goes back. Settings → Sessions → Tile order can put the agents waiting for you first.
tips.tilesView.title: See a whole team at once as tiles
tips.triageReport.text: Tell the Assistant in QA triager mode what you did and saw, or paste a screenshot. It finds the cause in the code, checks for a card that already covers it (even one not merged yet), then files a card with the evidence.
tips.triageReport.title: Report a problem to the QA triager
tips.twoProviders.text: Agents in one project can use different providers: say a Codex reviewer next to a Claude Code agent. Hand Over to… passes work between them.
tips.twoProviders.title: Mix Claude Code and Codex
tips.ui.counter: {total, plural, one {Tip · {n, number} of #} other {Tip · {n, number} of #}}
tips.ui.showOnStart: Show a tip when Combwork starts
tips.ui.title: Tips
tips.unexpectedClose.text: If Combwork was ended without quitting (a crash, or something closed it), the next start says when it was last seen and which agents were running, with Resume All. Settings → Sessions → Resume agents after an unexpected close resumes them by itself.
tips.unexpectedClose.title: Know when Combwork closed unexpectedly
tips.unmerged.text: The agent's tab shows how many commits aren't merged yet, Merge… in its ⋯ menu says what is left, and Version Control → Changes shows everything the agent changed since it branched.
tips.unmerged.title: See what a worktree agent has to merge
tips.unusedWorktrees.text: Removed an agent but kept its worktree? Version Control → Changes opens on the worktrees no agent uses, saying who made each: open one to see its work and merge it, or remove the merged ones with their branches.
tips.unusedWorktrees.title: Tidy kept worktrees
tips.updateFromTarget.text: Version Control → Branches & remotes: a branch behind the target has Update. Merge the target in or rebase onto it, where the branch is checked out; a conflict is undone at once, naming its files.
tips.updateFromTarget.title: Bring a branch up to date with its target
tips.usageMoves.text: In Settings → Accounts & Connections, open an account’s ⋯ → Account Settings… and tick When it reaches 98% of its weekly limit, move its agents to another account: they move once their turn is over and carry on there.
tips.usageMoves.title: Move agents before a plan runs out
tips.versionControlSwitch.text: Click None or Git atop a project’s Version Control tab to switch it from its next card; cards in flight keep the old rules. Each keeps its own workflow options, and when the folder changes (git init, say), Combwork offers the switch there.
tips.versionControlSwitch.title: Switch between None and Git
tips.versionControlTab.text: A project’s Version Control tab says what Combwork found in its folder, and starts with Workflow: who reviews, which checks pass first and who merges. Its header names the preset, and a click on it opens them.
tips.versionControlTab.title: One tab for version control and workflow
tips.viewerTokens.text: An app that shows what your agents are doing, such as Apiary, needs only a viewer token: Settings → Agent API → Viewer tokens makes one that can read everything and change nothing, and revokes it again.
tips.viewerTokens.title: Let another app watch Combwork
tips.workflowDefaults.text: Settings → Version Control sets the options every project starts from: Combwork defaults, for every workspace, and the open workspace’s over them. A project’s own options still win, and saving lists the projects that inherit the change.
tips.workflowDefaults.title: Set a workflow once for every project
tips.workflowOptions.text: Version Control → Workflow sets who reviews a card’s work, which checks pass first and who merges it. Pick a preset, or set each option: a change applies from the next card that starts.
tips.workflowOptions.title: Choose how cards get to Done
tips.workflowPresetsWhy.text: In Version Control → Workflow, click Solo, Pair or Team: it lists each option it sets and why, and marks what it would change. Nothing changes until you use it and save.
tips.workflowPresetsWhy.title: See what a preset does before you use it
tips.workspaceMoved.text: Moved the workspace folder, say to another drive? Open it from its new place and choose Repair… in the banner: agents' worktrees, their sessions, and Claude Code's conversations and memory follow it.
tips.workspaceMoved.title: Move a workspace without losing its agents
tips.workspaceMovedDefender.text: If Combwork had Defender skip the workspace's folders, Repair… after a move offers to move those exclusions to the new folders, with one administrator prompt, so none is left on a folder that's gone. Exclusions you made yourself stay as they are.
tips.workspaceMovedDefender.title: Defender exclusions follow a moved workspace
tips.workspaceNotes.text: Workspace notes, pinned first in Shared Notes, is for what's true of this machine, like a full path. Every agent gets it when it starts, in any folder, so it needn't go in a committed AGENTS.md. A section headed with a project's name is that project's alone.
tips.workspaceNotes.title: Notes about this machine for every agent
tips.waitingOnPurpose.title: A card that waits on purpose
tips.waitingOnPurpose.text: A card in Active held for a quiet window, or waiting for an answer? Right-click it, Mark as Waiting…, and say why: Combwork stops reporting it as stalled until you clear it or it leaves Active. Its agent keeps running.
